docs.title: Fundamental Concepts and ADT
docs.summary: Static vs. dynamic structures and the importance of Abstract Data Types (ADT) with Generics <T>.
docs.content: Data structures are organized ways to store and manipulate information in memory. Unlike static structures (such as fixed-size arrays), dynamic ones expand or contract according to execution needs. Thanks to TypeScript's use of generic types <T>, a node is not limited to storing primitives like integers or characters: it can hold complex objects, database records, or syntax tokens.
docs.realWorldUse: Creation of abstract data models and reusable libraries in professional software development.

docs.title: Stacks and the Call Stack
docs.summary: How the LIFO (Last In, First Out) structure manages function execution and syntax evaluation.
docs.content: Stacks are essential in low-level system design and compilers. Every time a program calls a function, the environment creates a 'Stack Frame' that stores local variables and the return address. In addition, they are used in syntax parsers for evaluating mathematical expressions (Infix to Postfix/Polish notation) and in the 'Undo/Redo' feature of code editors.
docs.realWorldUse: JavaScript V8 Engine (Call Stack), compiler parsers, Undo/Redo buttons.

docs.title: Queues, Deques, and Graph Algorithms
docs.summary: Use of the FIFO structure in algorithms like BFS and event-driven architectures.
docs.content: Queues and Double-Ended Queues (Deques) manage asynchronous data streams and task scheduling. They are the backbone of graph algorithms like BFS (Breadth-First Search) to find the shortest path in networks. In environments like Node.js and the browser, the Event Loop's 'Task Queue' manages I/O events in a non-blocking manner.
docs.realWorldUse: BFS algorithm in graphs/networks, Node.js Event Loop, print queues, and background tasks.

docs.title: Linked Lists and Memory Management
docs.summary: Heap memory management, dynamic pointers, and collision resolution.
docs.content: Linked Lists eliminate the need for contiguous memory blocks by reassigning `next` and `prev` pointers. In database building and operating systems, they are used to manage free blocks in the Heap and to resolve collisions in Hash Tables using the Chaining algorithm.
docs.realWorldUse: Memory allocators in C/C++, chaining in Hash Maps, music players (playlists).
